title.en: Format of the Statement of Profit and Loss

body.en: I Revenue from operations; II Other income; III Total income (I + II); IV Expenses: cost of materials consumed, purchases of stock-in-trade, changes in inventories of finished goods, WIP and stock-in-trade, employee benefits expense, finance costs, depreciation and amortisation expense, other expenses; V *Profit* before tax (III − IV); VI Tax expense; VII Profit for the period (V − VI).

narration.en: Let us work this out together, step by step.

say.en: Let us work this out together, step by step. Revenue from operations 20,00,000 rupees; other income 1,00,000 rupees; purchases of stock-in-trade 12,00,000 rupees; opening inventory 2,00,000 rupees; closing inventory 3,00,000 rupees; employee benefits 2,50,000 rupees; finance costs 50,000 rupees; depreciation 1,00,000 rupees; other expenses 1,50,000 rupees; tax 30 percent. Find profit for the period.
Total income equals 20,00,000 rupees plus 1,00,000 rupees equals 21,00,000 rupees.
Changes in inventories equals 2,00,000 rupees minus 3,00,000 rupees equals (1,00,000 rupees).
Total expenses equals 12,00,000 minus 1,00,000 plus 2,50,000 plus 50,000 plus 1,00,000 plus 1,50,000 equals 16,50,000 rupees.
Profit before tax equals 4,50,000 rupees; tax 30 percent equals 1,35,000 rupees; profit for the period equals 3,15,000 rupees.
So the answer is Profit for the period 3,15,000 rupees.
